why: the CBS takeover item mixes a staged sub change with many replies testing and revealing whether it is an April Fools joke.

why.T3-016: Members ask for the story behind the unexplained posts and one explains the giant pixel board and five-minute turns; the dismissals are rejection but the item's doing is asking and explaining what the event is.

why.T3-001: Members post a fake Discovery casting item as true and another knowingly clicks the bait, so the room stages its own April Fools fake rather than testing an outside claim.

why.T3-014: Members ask for a Discord, download it, gather in the server, and coordinate art and maintenance bots there; the target and alliance talk is subordinate to moving the room's planning into a chat.

why.T3-023: Moderators announce the sub is owned by CBS, sell All Access flair, promise delayed releases, and require a Bakula Q&A, staging a whole-sub April Fools takeover that members play inside.
why.T3-095: Members explicitly ask whether the CBS takeover is an April Fools thing, call it a joke, realize the AMA is an April Fools trick, and ask how the joke got stickied, testing the claim rather than merely playing the takeover.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: A single T3-023 placement would carry the staged CBS takeover and play but fail to carry the explicit separate thread of members testing and revealing whether the CBS ownership claim is an April Fools joke.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0338314 asks whether the CBS takeover is an April Fools thing, C0934207 calls it a joke, and C0072852 realizes the AMA is an April Fools trick, satisfying T3-095's gate for working out whether the claim is a joke.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-095 if forced to one; the staged takeover remains, but the testing/reveal layer is lost.

why.T3-009: The item leads with 'They did it' and 'We did it r/startrek!' and an invitation after completion; progress and dead reports are present, but the qualifying gate is marking the room's finished work as achieved.

why.T3-051: A member asks for upvotes to make Broccoli the first Google image result; this is a vote drive for a post to climb a search result, with no tile or canvas placement offered.

why.T3-070: Members supply a bitmap, updated guide, mission coordinates, direct links, pictures, borders, and the final Enterprise image; these are directions and materials for placers to follow, not merely an invitation to a sub or a call for hands.

why.T3-021: Members protect and defend the builds over hours, fix borders and middle pixels, and report gray filling in; the griefing is handled as upkeep and repair, not an alarm-led fight against a named attack.

why.T3-015: A moderator consolidates the flood of help requests into one post and announces removal of further help threads; this gathers canvas talk into one place rather than applying a general posting rule.

why.T3-004: Members argue which comm badge design to make, with one preferring TNG and another preferring DS9/VOY and suggesting the other be organized elsewhere; this is settling the mark's look.

why.T3-178: A member asks others to screw with Garrett Wang on Twitter for April Fools; this targets one named person on another site, not a canvas work, rival sub, or official joke.

why.T3-100: Members ask the mods to keep the April Fools ship design and leave it as the banner; later screenshot and archive requests concern preserving the same April Fools change after it was reverted.

why.T3-021: Members protect and defend the builds over hours, fix borders and middle pixels, and report gray filling in; the griefing is handled as upkeep and repair, not an alarm-led fight against a named attack.

why.T3-024: The room moves Enterprise left to avoid smushing others' hard work, relocates after seeing Jeep actively worked on, and warns against starting a war it cannot win; these are the room's own restraint toward neighbours' space, not an agreed border or truce.
